conclusion.root_cause: Not a broken prompt; the test expectation does not match the lobby design. The Mission Board prompt ('Pick a call', BoardPrompt) works. A client trigger fires Triggered on the client, and a server-side listener also saw it exactly once, from the right player. The prompt is enabled, has hold=0, and is within range. Its job is only to open the LobbyUI mission picker; it does not start a round. Under LobbyConfig.UseLobby=true, a round starts only when a player stands on a SquadPad, becomes squad leader, the countdown reaches 0 and LobbyService:Launch calls MissionService:StartMission. The tester triggered the board, never joined a pad and never chose a call, so InstanceId and SquadId stayed empty. That is why no fire, rescue or round counters appeared, only lobby and city counters. For a real player, or a bot that steps on a pad after picking a call, the flow works. I did not read the board handler body or run the pad-launch path end to end, so the picker-only behaviour is inferred from the file header and the probes. If the board should start a round by itself, LobbyService's board handler would need to launch the leader's squad after Choose, but that is a design change.
conclusion.evidence: Probe 4: the client prompt fired (fired=true) from 8 studs, but InstanceId and SquadId stayed empty. Probes 6 and 7: the server listener recorded BoardTrig=1 for xXBeansTitanXx, so the trigger reaches the server. LobbyUI showed Picker visible and no Squad panel or Banner. Probe 5: the board is tagged MissionBoard, has a ClickDetector, and UseLobby=true. The three SquadPad parts exist, and launching is driven by pad countdowns per the LobbyService header.
conclusion.fix_hint: No code fix is needed for the prompt. The test or bot should step onto a SquadPad (or call LobbyService._join and _launch) after picking a call. If a one-click start is wanted, make the board's Choose path call LobbyService:Launch for the player's squad, auto-joining a pad when the player has none.

--!strict
-- LobbyService [owner: G3]. The fire station is the LOBBY. Players spawn on the StationSpawn pads.
-- A big Mission Board (tag MissionBoard: SurfaceGui + ProximityPrompt + ClickDetector) lists
-- MissionCatalog; 3 glowing queue pads (tag SquadPad, attr PadId) on the apron each show their
-- squad's call + "2/4 READY". Stepping on a pad joins its squad; the first player on a pad starts a
-- countdown (LobbyConfig.CountdownSeconds, cut to FullCountdownSeconds when the squad is full, reset
-- when the pad empties). At 3..2..1 the station alarm lamps flash; at 0 the alarm blares and the
-- squad launches into its OWN mission instance (MissionService:StartMission), so several pads count
-- down and launch in parallel. On MissionService.MissionEnded the squad comes home ("Welcome back,
-- heroes (mostly)"). Idle fun: slide the fire pole, ring the bell, honk truck 67; standing still
-- labels you "on coffee break". Queue/countdown rules live in the pure ReplicatedStorage/Lobby/LobbyQueue.
-- LobbyConfig.UseLobby = false keeps v1's single auto-round (remotes are still declared).

-- Public API (contract, docs/game/03-tech-architecture.md §10 "v1.5 additions"):
--   LobbyService:GetSquads(): { Types.Squad }
--   LobbyService:GetSquad(squadId: string): Types.Squad?
--   LobbyService:Join(player: Player, padId: number): string?     -- squadId; first on a pad leads
--   LobbyService:Leave(player: Player)

conclusion.root_cause: Mostly a testing artefact, plus a small placement flaw. Pathfinding itself works in the lobby. Targets at floor level next to the board (y=1.5, z=164 to 180) all return Success, and so do routes into the plaza. The NoPath results come from the Mission Board target point, (-40, 6.25, 170). That point is the pivot of the MissionBoard model, which has no BaseParts, and it sits about 5 studs above the walkable floor (y~0.5-1) and under the BoardHeader. PathfindingService cannot snap a goal in mid-air or inside geometry to the navmesh, so it returns NoPath. Floor-level goals at the same x/z succeed except a single y=3.8 probe at z=170, which is also inside or above the board geometry. Bots that aim at the prompt anchor therefore get NoPath or stop short. A real player walks up to the prompt (MaxActivationDistance 16) without any pathfinding, so the prompt is reachable. The fix is to put the board's prompt and anchor on a real, floor-anchored part, or have callers target a floor-level standing point.
conclusion.evidence: Path from the player to the MissionBoard pivot (-40,6.25,170) gave NoPath for AgentRadius 2, 3 and 4. Targets at (-40, 1.5, z) for z=164,166,168,170,172,175,180 all returned Success, and (-40,3.8,165) also succeeded. Only the elevated points near z=170 failed. MissionBoard has zero BasePart descendants, so the prompt's position is just a model pivot at y=6.25. BoardHeader (y~12) sits above it, and the lobby floor is at y~0.5.
conclusion.fix_hint: In StationBuilder, give MissionBoard a real anchored base part (CanCollide true or an Attachment) at floor level and parent BoardPrompt to it, and expose a floor-level approach point, for example 4 to 6 studs in front of the board at y~1. Bots and testers should path to that point instead of the elevated pivot.

for _,z in ipairs({164,166,168,170,172,175,180}) do
 for _,y in ipairs({1.5,3.8}) do

 end
